evidence.description: The public state getter directly reads and sorts items.
Changes schedule a state read on the main queue rather than the background queue.
needsUpdate reads items directly before load schedules its background work.

candidates.explanation: The background queue mutates items, while publication reads state on the main queue and public state access and load's needsUpdate check read items without using that queue. The serial background queue therefore does not protect all accesses, allowing concurrent reads and writes to the same Set.
candidates.title: Shared items are read and written without consistent synchronization

evidence.description: The network error is ignored and decoding failure returns without reporting a failure.
Cache reading and decoding errors are suppressed by try?.
Encoding and writing errors are swallowed by an empty catch block.

candidates.explanation: The network callback ignores its error, decoding failures become silent returns, restoration errors are suppressed, and persistence errors are caught with an empty body. These paths provide no error signal or diagnostic, making failed operations indistinguishable from operations that simply produce no update.
candidates.title: Loading and persistence failures are silently discarded

evidence.description: Downloaded items are cleaned and merged without checking their language.
Restored items are explicitly filtered by the current language.
Cleaning changes only text and does not filter by language.

candidates.explanation: Restoration excludes news whose language differs from Language.current, but downloading adds all decoded news without the same restriction. Consequently, downloaded news can be published and saved even though those same entries would be discarded on restoration, making the available news depend on how it was loaded.
candidates.title: Language filtering differs between downloaded and restored news
